decisions.rationale: dataset.duplicate_row_rate is 0.0 over row_count 166158, so no exact duplicate rows exist in bronze and no dedupe step is proposed.

One row is a scheduled flight leg: year/month/day (null_rate 0.0 each), carrier (16 distinct, null_rate 0.0), flight (2994 distinct, null_rate 0.0), origin (EWR/JFK/LGA) and sched_dep_time (969 distinct, null_rate 0.0) are the smallest all-required set that plausibly identifies a row; a reviewer must measure uniqueness in the warehouse before approval.
_airbyte_raw_id, _airbyte_extracted_at and _airbyte_meta all carry is_airbyte_metadata true and are dropped as capture-tool columns.

Every numeric column lands as DECIMAL(38,9) but all mins, maxes and sample_values are integral (for example distance min 80.0 max 4983.0, hour distinct_values 5.0 through 23.0), so each is cast to INTEGER.

dep_time, sched_dep_time, arr_time and sched_arr_time range between 1.0 and 2400.0, an HHMM clock encoding rather than a duration or timestamp, so they stay INTEGER and are not converted to a time type.
time_hour sample_values are uniformly ISO-8601 with a Z offset (2013-01-01T10:00:00Z and similar) at null_rate 0.0, justifying a strict VARCHAR to TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE cast.
dep_time and dep_delay (null_rate 0.029388), arr_time (0.0307), and arr_delay and air_time (0.032981) keep their nulls; no row is dropped and no value is imputed.
tailnum has null_count 1521 (null_rate 0.009154) across 3825 distinct values, so it is retained nullable rather than required.
is_missing_departure is derived from dep_time being null (4883 rows, null_rate 0.029388) so consumers can filter these rows deliberately instead of inferring them.

purpose: silver_nyc_flights is the cleaned, contract-typed view of bronze.nyc_flights: 166158 NYC-origin flight legs for 2013 months 1 through 6, with capture metadata removed, DECIMAL(38,9) measures narrowed to INTEGER, and the ISO-8601 time_hour string cast to a timestamp. It feeds downstream on-time-performance and carrier/route aggregates.
usage: Read one row as one scheduled flight leg keyed by year, month, day, carrier, flight, origin and sched_dep_time. Clock-style columns (dep_time, sched_dep_time, arr_time, sched_arr_time) are HHMM integers between 1 and 2400, not durations, while dep_delay, arr_delay and air_time are signed or positive minutes. Consumers computing completion or delay statistics should filter deliberately on is_missing_departure or on null arr_delay rather than treating nulls as zero.
limitations: Null departure and arrival measures are retained, not resolved: dep_time and dep_delay are null for 2.9388% of rows, arr_time for 3.07%, and arr_delay and air_time for 3.2981%, and the profile carries no cancellation column to explain them. tailnum is null for 0.9154% of rows. The HHMM clock integers are not converted into real timestamps because no timezone-resolved departure instant is present beyond the hourly time_hour. The declared grain is asserted from column-level evidence only; the profile reports duplicate_row_rate 0.0 for whole rows but does not prove uniqueness of the grain key set, so a reviewer must verify it.
